evidence_and_scope.change_required: Allow the existing Users.username column to be NULL so registration can persist the four-field public request without inventing a username.
out_of_scope: No new request or response fields
No table, relationship, ownership, cascade, index, or uniqueness changes
No changes to legacy login behavior

columns.constraint_and_index: Preserve the existing unique constraint; MySQL permits multiple NULL values in a unique index.
columns.source_rationale: UC-01 and its approved API contract do not accept username, and the prompt explicitly prohibits inventing one. The current NOT NULL mapping otherwise makes persistence impossible.

relationships_and_ownership.statement: The proposal does not alter ownership or relationships. Existing user-owned resources remain scoped by the authenticated user in their respective implementations.

sensitive_data_and_exposure.credential_storage: Password remains bcrypt-hashed; confirmPassword and plaintext credentials are never persisted.
sensitive_data_and_exposure.default_selection: No selection behavior changes are proposed.
sensitive_data_and_exposure.logging_and_export: Do not log or export passwords, confirmPassword, password hashes, or access tokens.

migration_plan.name: 20260831095333-make-users-username-nullable.ts
forward_operations: Alter Users.username from VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL to VARCHAR(255) NULL while preserving its unique constraint.
rollback_operations: Refuse rollback while any Users row has username IS NULL.
After an explicit data-resolution decision, alter Users.username back to VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL while preserving uniqueness.
migration_plan.data_loss_risk: The forward migration is non-destructive. Rollback is blocked if registrations created under this contract have NULL usernames; no automatic or invented backfill is permitted.
migration_plan.deployment_considerations: The ALTER may take a metadata or table lock depending on MySQL state and table size; apply through the repository migration mechanism during an approved maintenance window.

assumptions: The existing physical table and column names are Users.username as declared by the current TypeORM entity.
The existing unique constraint on username is retained so non-null legacy usernames remain unique.
Nullable username is the smallest compatible schema change; making username non-unique, renaming the table, or replacing legacy username login is not authorized by UC-01.
No automatic username backfill may be derived from email or fullName because the approved prompt prohibits invented username values.

approval.approved_via: researcher confirmation in active Codex session

pending_amendment.trigger_evidence: A rebuilt backend repeatedly fails migration startup with TypeORMError: Table Users does not exist; the physical vibe_business database contains no Users table available to the migration.
pending_amendment.required_change: Extend migration 20260831095333 so that, when Users is absent, it creates the existing entity-mapped Users table instead of attempting changeColumn. When Users already exists, retain the previously approved nullable-username alteration path.

migration_behavior.forward: Inspect Users. Create the table exactly from the current entity mapping only when absent; otherwise apply the approved nullable username change. Preserve synchronize=false.
migration_behavior.rollback: If this migration created an otherwise absent Users table, rollback would drop a potentially populated table and is therefore destructive; refuse automatic rollback once any row exists. The existing-table path retains the previously approved guarded rollback.
migration_behavior.data_risk: Forward creation is additive. Dropping a populated table is prohibited without separate destructive authorization.
out_of_scope: No Accounts, Bills, Goals, Transactions or Categories table creation
No relationship, ownership, cascade or public API change
No database volume reset or data deletion

approval.resolution: Read-only metadata inspection confirmed the approved physical table already exists as lowercase users with id and password_hash. No table creation is required; repair is limited to source mapping alignment and the previously approved nullable-username alteration.
